blocks.alt: Five rounded boxes stacked vertically and joined by downward arrows: yellow (mass of known solid, volume of known gas or molar concentration of known solution), green (calculate moles of the known using the relevant formula), red (ratio of known and unknown from the balanced equation), blue (moles of the unknown using the relevant formula) and orange (convert moles of the unknown to mass, volume or concentration).
blocks.caption: Approach to do stoichiometric calculations (original drawing after the scheme printed on p82 of the textbook).
blocks.long_description: Box 1: Mass of known solid or volume of a known gas, or molar concentration of known solution. Box 2: Calculate number of moles of known solid or volume of a known gas, or molar concentration of known solution using the relevant formula. Box 3: Find the ratio of the known and the unknown reactant or product from the balanced chemical equation. Box 4: Calculate the number of moles of the unknown reactant or product using the relevant formula. Box 5: Convert the number of moles of the unknown to mass, volume, or concentration of the substance.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed third box reads “unknow”; the word is unknown.
Sample Problem 4.11 (Mole-Mole Conversion)
When 3.3 mole of nitrogen reacts with hydrogen to form ammonia, how many moles of hydrogen are consumed in the process? The equation for this reaction is
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g)
Solution:
Number of moles of N₂ = 3.3 mol
Number of moles of H₂ = ?
1 mole of N₂ needs H₂ to produce NH₃ = 3/1 = 3mol
3.6 moles of N₂ needs H₂ to produce NH₃ = 3 × 3.3 = 9.9 mol

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question gives 3.3 mol of N₂, not 3.6 moles; 3.3 mol of N₂ needs 3 × 3.3 = 9.9 mol of H₂, as calculated.
Quick Check 4.5

blocks.prompt:
How many moles of carbon dioxide are produced when 2.25 moles of glucose are used by a person? The oxygen is in excess. The equation for the reaction is:
C₆H₁₂O₆(s) + 6O₂(g) → 6CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l)
blocks.explanation: In the equation, 1 mol of glucose gives 6 mol of CO₂. So 2.25 × 6 = 13.5 mol of CO₂ are produced.

blocks.text: Sample Problem 4.12 (Mass-Mass Conversion)
Calculate the mass of Al needed to react completely with 32.0 g of iron (III) oxide according to the equation given below:
2Al(s) + Fe₂O₃(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(s).
Solution:
Molar mass of Fe₂O₃, M = 159.6 g mol⁻¹
Number of moles of Fe₂O₃ (n) = m/M = 32.0 g / 159.6 g mol⁻¹ = 0.02 mol
From the balanced equation, 1 mol of Fe₂O₃ reacts with 2 moles of Al, therefore, number of moles of Al that reacts with 0.02 mole of Fe₂O₃ = 2 x 0.02 = 0.04 mol
Mass of Al = n x M = 0.04 mol x 27 g mol⁻¹

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: 32.0 / 159.6 = 0.200 mol of Fe₂O₃, not 0.02 mol. So Al = 2 × 0.200 = 0.400 mol, and the mass of Al = 0.400 mol × 27 g mol⁻¹ = 10.8 g, not 1.08 g.
Quick Check 4.6

blocks.prompt:
Fe₂O₃, an ore of iron is called Hematite. CO can reduce it to get free Fe as below:
Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g)
How much Fe can be produced from 160 g of Fe₂O₃?
blocks.explanation: Moles of Fe₂O₃ = 160 ÷ 159.6 = 1.0 mol. In the equation, 1 mol of Fe₂O₃ gives 2 mol of Fe. Mass of Fe = 2.0 × 55.8 = about 112 g.

blocks.text: Sample Problem 4.13 (Volume-Volume)
Calculate volume of ammonia that can be produced by the reaction of 100 dm³ of hydrogen with excess of nitrogen at STP? The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g)
Solution:
Volume of hydrogen = 100 dm³
Volume of ammonia = ?
67.2 dm³ (3 mol) of H₂ produce ammonia = 44.8 dm³ (2 mol)
1 dm³ of H₂ produce ammonia = 44.8/67.2 = 2/3
100 dm³ of H₂ produce ammonia = 2/3 x 100 = 66.7 dm³
So, the volume of ammonia produced by the reaction of 100 dm³ of H₂ with excess nitrogen is 66.7 dm³.
Quick Check 4.7

blocks.prompt:
Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide produced at STP when 4.5 dm³ of methane is burnt by a person. The oxygen is in excess. The equation for the reaction is:
CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g)
blocks.explanation: In the equation, 1 mol of CH₄ gives 1 mol of CO₂; for gases the volume ratio is the same, 1 : 1. So 4.5 dm³ of CO₂ is produced.

blocks.text: Sample Problem 4.14 Mole-Mass calculations

Solid lithium hydroxide LiOH is used in space vehicles. It is employed to remove exhaled carbon dioxide from the living environment by forming solid lithium carbonate and liquid water. Calculate the mass of Li₂CO₃ that can be produced by 20.0 mol of LiOH.
2LiOH(s) + CO₂(g) → Li₂CO₃(s) + H₂O(l)
Solution:
According to the given balanced chemical equation,
2 moles of LiOH produces = 1 mole Li₂CO₃
20.0 moles of LiOH produces = 1/2 × 20.0 = 10.0 mol Li₂CO₃
Mass of Li₂CO₃ produced = No. of mole × Molar mass
Mass of Li₂CO₃ produced = 10.0 mol × 73.9 g mol⁻¹ = 739.0 g
Thus, 739.0 g Li₂CO₃ will be produced from 20.0 moles of LiOH.
Quick Check 4.8

blocks.prompt:
Calculate the mass of sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), a household bleach, produced by the reaction of 2.25 moles of chlorine with excess sodium hydroxide. The balanced equation is
2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) → NaOCl(aq) + NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l)
blocks.explanation: In the equation, 1 mol of Cl₂ gives 1 mol of NaOCl. Molar mass of NaOCl = 23 + 16 + 35.5 = 74.5 g/mol. Mass = 2.25 × 74.5 = 167.6 g.

blocks.text: Sample Problem 4.15 (Mass-mole calculations)
Baking soda (NaHCO₃) acts as an antacid. It can neutralize excess hydrochloric acid (HCl) secreted by the stomach according to equation.
NaHCO₃(g) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(aq)
How many moles of HCl will be neutralized by 2.1 g of baking soda
Solution:
Molar mass of NaHCO₃ = 84.0 g mol⁻¹
Moles of NaHCO₃ = 2.1 g / 84.0 g mol⁻¹ = 0.025 mol
Stoichiometrically, the mole ratio of HCl and NaHCO₃ is 1 : 1.
Hence moles of HCl used = 0.025 mol
Thus 2.1 g of NaHCO₃ will neutralize 0.025 moles of HCl.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Baking soda is a solid, not a gas: the reactant is NaHCO₃(s), not NaHCO₃(g). NaHCO₃(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g).
Sample Problem 4.16 (Mass-Volume Conversion)
What volume of hydrogen at STP will be produced when 7.0 g of iron are reacted with an excess of sulphuric acid?
Fe(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + H₂(g)
Solution:
Molar mass of Fe (M) = 55.8 g/mol
Number of moles of iron (n) = m/M = 7.0 g / 55.8 gmol⁻¹ = 0.125 mol
From the balanced equation, 1 mol of iron produces 1 mole of hydrogen.
So, number of moles of H₂ = 0.125 mol
Volume of H₂ in dm³ = molar volume x moles of H₂ = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ x 0.125 mol
= 2.8 dm³
